decision: dmg window-training strategy reusable, engineering work remains

engineering_bottleneck_ranking.impact: Consumes 72.6% to 74.4% of steady-state training step time (3.47s / 2.63s). The 730-step Python iteration loop is the primary forward cost.
Consumes 25.3% to 26.8% of steady-state training step time (1.28s / 0.89s). Inductor autograd executes efficiently on CUDA at B=100 with Bwd/Fwd ratio of 0.34x to 0.37x.
Peak allocated VRAM is only 469.0 MB on a 12GB GPU (>96% headroom). Memory is not a constraint at B=100.

executive_summary.b100_feasibility: Fully validated and stable. Peak VRAM is 469.0 MB (< 4% of 12GB GPU), zero OOM, finite gradients (norm ~32.8), and clean backward BPTT.
executive_summary.dmg_inheritance: The 730d (365 warmup + 365 scored) random window sampling from dmg is directly reusable in Auto-FUSE, saving 5.0x wall-clock and 5.0x VRAM over full-period training.
executive_summary.speed_metrics: B=100 steady-state training step takes 4.78s (Structure 2) and 3.53s (Structure 8), delivering 753.1 to 1019.1 steps/hour and 15,271 to 20,665 basin-days/s. Forward = 3.47s (Structure 2) / 2.63s (Structure 8), Backward = 1.28s (Structure 2) / 0.89s (Structure 8) with Bwd/Fwd ratio = 0.34x to 0.37x.
executive_summary.structure_batching_rule: Fix structure s per mini-batch to preserve fullgraph vmap compilation across the 100 basin-time windows.
